items.question: What is this knowledge called for the dear one?
premises: It is addressed to the dear one.
items.inference: This knowledge is an all-disease-destroying, health-giving gift for the dear one.
uncertainties: Gender and case of vidyārogyapradaṃ inferred from context.
items.plain_english: This is all-disease-destroying and knowledge-and-health-giving, dear one.

items.question: What fruit is declared from sattvic meditation?
premises: The fruit is born of sattvic meditation.
The address is to the goddess.
items.inference: The declared fruit arises from sattvic meditation.
uncertainties: Exact sandhi split of phalametad is editorially fused.
items.plain_english: This fruit, born of sattvic meditation, is declared, O goddess.

items.question: What fortune becomes available by this rite?
premises: The result becomes for the goddess.
items.inference: By this rite incomparable fortune becomes.
uncertainties: Case of saubhāgyamatulaṃ inferred as accusative.
items.plain_english: By this rite, O goddess, incomparable fortune becomes.

items.question: Who becomes ageless and immortal?
premises: That one becomes ageless and immortal.
The subject is introduced by who.
items.inference: Whoever meditates on the seed becomes ageless and immortal.
uncertainties: Optative force rendered as future-like result.
items.plain_english: Whoever meditates on the seed becomes ageless and immortal.

items.question: By whom is the clan leader worshipped?
premises: The goddesses reside in six supports.
The address is to the clan leader.
items.inference: The clan leader is worshipped by the six-support-residing goddesses.
uncertainties: Instrumental plural feminine inferred from ending.
items.plain_english: O clan leader, you are worshipped by the goddesses residing in the six supports.

items.question: What does the supreme prāsāda seed resemble?
premises: The adjective agrees with the seed.
items.inference: The supreme prāsāda seed resembles young red.
uncertainties: Accusative agreement inferred from adjective ending.
items.plain_english: The supreme prāsāda seed resembles young red.

items.question: By what is it surrounded?
premises: The address is to the mother.
items.inference: It is surrounded by twenty-five touch-letters, O mother.
uncertainties: Antecedent of saṃvītam is not explicit in this verse.
items.plain_english: It is surrounded by twenty-five touch-letters, O mother.

items.question: How should the self be remembered?
premises: The remembering is by immovable inner self.
The address is to the goddess.
items.inference: One should remember the self with an immovable inner self.
uncertainties: ātmānañca may be accusative object of smared.
items.plain_english: O goddess, one should remember the self with an immovable inner self.

items.question: What should the wise one chant?
premises: The number is one thousand eight.
items.inference: The wise one should chant a maṇḍala one thousand eight times.
uncertainties: aṣṭottarasahasrantu may modify repetition count rather than maṇḍala.
items.plain_english: The wise one should chant the maṇḍala one thousand eight times.

items.question: Who are made subject in this list?
premises: Sages, yakṣas, nāgas, apsarasas, and women are listed.
items.inference: The listed beings are the ones made subject.
uncertainties: The governing verb appears in the next verse.
items.plain_english: Vidyādharas, sages, yakṣas, nāgas, apsarasas, and women.

items.question: What does he make subjugated without doubt?
premises: Humans and others are also included.
items.inference: He makes them subjugated without doubt, and humans too.
uncertainties: Pronoun antecedent for karoti is supplied from context.
items.plain_english: He makes them subjugated without doubt; what then of humans and others?

items.question: Who becomes forcibly subjugated from chanting?
items.inference: From chanting, remembering on the head, he becomes forcibly subjugated.
uncertainties: The exact referent of yasya is not explicit.
items.plain_english: Remembering on the head, from chanting he becomes forcibly subjugated.
